blocked.title: When does adding a relevant procedural memory retract an otherwise correct action under a frozen executor?

audited.title: When does adding a relevant procedural memory retract an otherwise correct action under a frozen executor?

candidate.title: When does adding a relevant procedural memory retract an otherwise correct action under a frozen executor?

source_a.title: Towards a Formal Definition of Agent Memory: Basis, Span, Optimality, and the Sequential Memory Problem
source_a.claim: The formal memory framework explicitly assumes self-containment ('storing an event never throws it away') and monotonicity ('more memory is never worse, so coverage is non-decreasing in the stored set').

source_b.title: Agent Skills Can Be Harmful: An Empirical Study of Skill-Induced Failures in LLM Agents
source_b.claim: Differential attribution on SkillsBench and SWE-Skills-Bench identifies 307 skill-induced failures, including 125 functional failures and 182 efficiency regressions; Task-Implementation Fault accounts for 86 of 125 functional failures, and seemingly relevant skills often make agents incorrectly implement or omit task-required elements.

empirical_evidence.relation: Source A supplies an explicit operational monotonicity assumption for stored memory. Source B supplies scope-linked empirical violations in which an added procedural memory/skill, compared against a no-skill or semantically matched reference run on the same task, causes functional failure or cost regression under a frozen inference-time executor.

lane_evidence.assumption: For an agent memory system, storing an additional event or memory item should not remove it and should not make coverage/answerability worse: more memory is never worse.
lane_evidence.violation: Loaded skills are persistent procedural memory items supplied at inference time, yet paired differential runs attribute 125 functional failures and 182 efficiency regressions to those added skills; 68.8% of functional failures are Task-Implementation Faults where seemingly relevant skills induce incorrect implementation or omission of required elements.
lane_evidence.scope_link: The violated scope is bounded to frozen-executor, inference-time procedural memory use on the same task, where the paired reference run solves the task or solves it more cheaply. This does not claim a violation for parameter training, semantic factual coverage alone, or unmatched tasks.

candidate.irreducible_object: A retraction boundary for procedural memory admission: the conditions under which an added, seemingly relevant procedure changes the executor's action selection so that a previously correct required element is omitted or incorrectly implemented, despite the stored item remaining available and semantically relevant.

mature_theory_baselines.name: Coverage-monotonic memory theory
mature_theory_baselines.same_information_projection: Represent each loaded skill as an additional event/procedure in the stored set and project task success into answerability/coverage of required task elements.
mature_theory_baselines.ex_ante_prediction: Adding a skill cannot reduce the set of covered required elements; any observed failure must come from an item that was absent, irrelevant, or outside the memory span.
mature_theory_baselines.distinguishing_prediction: A paired same-task run can identify cases where the no-skill executor includes the required element, the skill-guided executor omits or incorrectly implements it, and the added skill is semantically relevant rather than obviously unrelated.
mature_theory_baselines.cannot_express: It cannot express nonmonotonic retraction of an already-executed required element because its operational assumption makes coverage non-decreasing in the stored set.
mature_theory_baselines.exact_reduction_test: Use paired frozen-executor runs with identical task, tools, budget, and scoring; vary only whether the attributed procedural skill is loaded. If the no-skill run satisfies the required element and the skill run omits or incorrectly implements it while provenance shows the skill was invoked, coverage-monotonic memory theory fails the exact cell.

mature_theory_baselines.name: Nonmonotonic belief revision / default logic
mature_theory_baselines.same_information_projection: Treat the skill as a default rule or conditional procedure that can override prior behavior when its trigger conditions match the task context.
mature_theory_baselines.ex_ante_prediction: A newly added rule can retract a prior conclusion or action when the rule's applicability condition is triggered and has priority over the old default.
mature_theory_baselines.distinguishing_prediction: The empirical object should expose a procedural applicability-boundary variable: not merely semantic relevance, but whether the skill's trigger/preconditions license replacing or omitting a task-required step.
mature_theory_baselines.cannot_express: Generic belief revision can say that retraction happened, but it does not by itself identify which observable procedural-boundary features distinguish harmful overriding from benign specialization in agent skill execution.
mature_theory_baselines.exact_reduction_test: Encode the paired skill/no-skill traces as defaults with explicit trigger, priority, and conflict information. If the same observable trigger/priority information predicts exactly which added skills retract required steps, the case reduces to nonmonotonic belief revision; if paired traces with matched trigger/conflict information still split by an independently measured procedural applicability-boundary feature, the reduction fails.

same_information_nonreducibility.claim: The surviving problem is not 'skills can hurt' but the missing operational boundary at which an added relevant procedure licenses suppression of a task-required action in a frozen executor.
same_information_nonreducibility.why_each_baseline_cannot_express_predict: Coverage-monotonic memory theory predicts the wrong sign for the paired skill-induced omission cases. Generic nonmonotonic reasoning can represent retraction after the fact, but the supplied evidence does not yet provide an observable applicability-boundary variable that predicts when relevant procedural memory will retract required behavior; therefore it cannot be accepted as a complete same-information reduction without the exact trace-encoding test.

candidate.exact_prediction: Under a frozen executor, identical task statement, tool set, scoring contract, and budget, loading a semantically relevant procedural skill will sometimes cause the agent to omit or incorrectly implement an element that the paired no-skill run correctly includes; the harmful cases should be predictable from a procedural applicability-boundary feature rather than from relevance, prompt length, or task difficulty alone.
candidate.strongest_same_information_baseline: Nonmonotonic belief revision/default-rule priority, given the same trace, skill text, trigger conditions, and task-required-element labels.

domain_transfer_audit.mature_source_domain: Formal agent memory and nonmonotonic reasoning
domain_transfer_audit.why_not_domain_transfer: The target object is not a rename of belief revision. It concerns executable procedural memory in agent trajectories, where the disputed event is an action-sequence change: a required implementation element present under no-skill disappears or is incorrectly implemented after a relevant skill is loaded. The empirical attribution is paired and executor-frozen, making the causal surface narrower than generic nonmonotonic reasoning.

rejected_patterns.reason: The source evidence is not merely retrieved experience failing to change behavior; it is paired evidence that an added procedural artifact changes behavior enough to cause attributed functional failure or efficiency regression.
The object is not a sparse validation/filtering tradeoff; the compared runs differ by loaded procedural memory, not by validation-set size or filter selectivity.
The issue is not a valid scaffold that remains inactive. The attributed failures involve skill-guided runs where the skill causally shapes execution relative to a no-skill or matched-skill reference.

candidate.cheapest_problem_falsifier: Materialize paired frozen-executor cells from the released skill-failure attribution setting: same task, tools, budget, scorer, and base model, with only skill presence varied. If all harmful cases are explained by obvious irrelevance, prompt length, task difficulty, or an explicit default-rule trigger/priority encoding with no residual applicability-boundary variable, the proposed problem is falsified.
candidate.endpoint_headroom_requirement: The no-skill or matched-skill reference must solve the task or solve it more cheaply, and the skill-guided run must have enough headroom to fail or regress on the same endpoint; aggregate-only improvements without paired harmful cells do not qualify.
